name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the system of equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-5y+7z=14 \\ -5x+6y+2z=9 \\ 3x-2y+4z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}$, where $D$ is the determinant of the coefficient matrix and ${D}_{z}=$
worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+(-5)y+7z=14 \\ -5x+6y+2z=9 \\ 3x+(-2)y+4z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
D=|\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 7 \\ -5 & 6 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{z}$, we replace the third column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 14 \\ -5 & 6 & 9 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We are given the system

{2x+(−5)y+7z=14−5x+6y+2z=93x+(−2)y+4z=1.

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

D=|2−57−5623−24|.

Now, to construct Dz, we replace the third column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

Dz=|2−514−5693−21|.
